newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels govt puts off Euro Parliament decision.
newsitem.headline: Brussels govt puts off Euro Parliament decision.

text.p: The Brussels Regional Government postponed on Thursday taking a decision on usage of a car park at the European Parliament's new billion-dollar headquarters building, a spokesman said on Thursday.
"A new proposal will be made to the government on (April 17)," Maurice Peeters, spokesman for Brussels Environment Minister Didier Gosuin told Reuters.

The European Parliament said last week it would refuse to take delivery of the 32 billion Belgian franc building from developers Forum Leopold SA unless they could deliver a permit from the Brussels government allowing full use of its underground, 2,300 place car park.
Delivery was due to take place this weekend. The Parliament must pay the developers 100 million francs for each month no lease has been signed.
Forum Leopold's main shareholders include Belgian utility holding company Tractebel, property company Immobel and Bacob bank.
Peeters declined to say whether Gosuin was proposing the government approve full use of the car park, or order - as he suggested earlier this year - part of it to be bricked up.
